description: Our team combines expertise in the space sector, artificial intelligence, and gamified visual elements to create a practical and rewarding experience, enabling astronauts to look after their health on a daily basis during missions.
summary:
CosmoMedic: Smarter Health Monitoring for Space Missions

Astronauts shouldn't have to spend more time managing their health data to stay healthy. CosmoMedic aims to make health monitoring simpler, more personalized, and less demanding through two complementary solutions: Orbi and the CosmoMedic Dashboard.

Orbi is an AI-powered health and wellness companion designed for astronauts. Through quick daily check-ins, voice-assisted interaction, personalized feedback, and gamification, it makes health tracking more accessible and engaging. By combining individual health histories with health indicators, Orbi aims to identify persistent changes, provide contextualized insights, and offer proactive support without replacing medical professionals.

CosmoMedic Dashboard supports medical teams on Earth by bringing crew health indicators, historical trends, flagged measurements, and data quality information into a unified view. It helps teams identify records requiring attention, reduce information fragmentation, and prepare more efficiently for medical assessments while preserving sensitive information.

Together, Orbi and CosmoMedic connect individual well-being with crew-level health oversight, aiming to reduce administrative effort, improve awareness, and support timely, informed human decisions.

Our mission: less time managing health data, more time focusing on what matters—exploration.

The Problem We're Solving

How can we make astronaut health monitoring more personal, less demanding, and better integrated into daily life in space?

Astronaut health monitoring involves multiple indicators, devices, and daily records. However, collecting information is only part of the challenge. Making it accessible, meaningful, and easy to manage is equally important.

CosmoMedic addresses this challenge by combining assisted data collection, personalized monitoring, and an interactive health companion in a single experience.

Our Solution: Meet Orbi and CosmoMedic Dashboard

Orbi is a personal health and wellness companion designed to transform how astronauts monitor their health.

Its value goes beyond simple automation. We recognize that every astronaut has a unique background and specific needs. Orbi leverages this personal history to identify significant changes and provide contextualized insights, while also taking into account the astronaut’s own self-reports and overall well-being.

Our goal is for astronauts to spend less time on health monitoring and gain greater clarity regarding their own condition—allowing them to remain focused on what truly matters: the mission.

Why Orbi Is Different

What if health monitoring required less effort from an astronaut, rather than more?
Our approach combines several key features:

  • A Check-in Designed for Under 5 Minutes: Data from devices and scheduled activities can pre-populate check-ins, allowing astronauts to simply confirm or correct the information.
  • Voice-Assisted Interaction: Orbi explores voice-based interaction to make daily health reporting more natural and accessible, reducing the need for manual input.
  • Connected health data: Backend support for wearable devices, blood pressure monitors, dosimeters, and other sensors.
  • Personalized monitoring: Historical indicators, trends, and persistent patterns provide context that goes beyond basic, isolated data points.
  • Proactive support: Significant changes can trigger targeted notifications and suggestions for follow-up consultations.
  • Gamification: Currencies, progress tracking, avatars, and achievements make daily engagement more rewarding.
  • Mission continuity: Backend synchronization mechanisms support offline logging and communication with ground control teams.

Why CosmoMedic Dashboard Matters

How can we ensure that important information regarding the crew's health is not lost amidst various measurements, incomplete records, and individual medical histories?

CosmoMedic tackles this challenge in two ways:

  • From fragmented data to a unified view: CosmoMedic brings together crew health indicators, measurement histories, and data quality information into a single dashboard, reducing the effort required to consolidate records and allowing medical teams to focus more on assessment and care.
  • From scattered alerts to targeted analysis: by highlighting measurements that are pending, outdated, or missing across the crew, CosmoMedic helps medical teams quickly identify which records require attention, facilitating more efficient follow-up—without, however, replacing clinical judgment.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Our goal is to reduce the time spent recording and interpreting health information, while encouraging consistent monitoring through an accessible and engaging experience.

For astronauts, this means fewer repetitive interactions, clearer insights into their own health, and a greater awareness of their personal trends.

For mission teams, organized records, medical summaries, and structured communication can facilitate more efficient health monitoring.

Our long-term objective is to explore how intelligent assistance can reduce the workload associated with monitoring during long-duration space missions, without replacing healthcare professionals.

Tools & Technologies

  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, REST APIs.
  • Frontend: React Native, Expo, TypeScript.
  • AI: CrewAI, Groq-hosted language models, rule-based monitoring.
  • Data: NASA OSDR, AGBRESA, synthetic longitudinal health records.
  • Integrations: Health Connect, HealthKit and Bluetooth Low Energy supported by backend telemetry interfaces; device synchronization simulated in the current frontend.
  • Other Technologies: Voice recognition and speech synthesis, offline synchronization mechanisms, FHIR medical data export.
  • Development: GitHub, collaborative design and development tools.

Team Considerations

  • Databases and Simulation:

To build our solution, we used real-world data from NASA’s Inspiration4 mission (OSD-569 and OSD-575), including hematological, metabolic, cardiovascular, and immunological assessments of four astronauts. We also incorporated data from the AGBRESA study, which monitored 24 volunteers during 60 days of bed rest to investigate certain effects of microgravity.

However, these datasets have limitations: Inspiration4 lacks continuous daily measurements, while AGBRESA was conducted on Earth and cannot fully replicate space conditions.

We turned these limitations into an opportunity for experimentation. We developed a synthetic 180-day mission involving four astronauts, with an additional 30-day pre-launch period. The simulation combines individual health profiles, research-informed physiological parameters, temporal variations, and controlled events, such as sleep disturbances and cardiovascular changes.

We acknowledge that synthetic data cannot replace clinical validation based on real-world data. Our goal is to demonstrate the technical feasibility of this approach, grounding it in scientific evidence while maintaining full transparency regarding the origin and limitations of the data.

The system distinguishes simulated from device-measured data and includes safeguards against unsupported medical advice. Its purpose is health awareness and support, not autonomous diagnosis.

Monitoring & AI Workflow

  1. Collect: Receive health records, check-ins, and device telemetry.
  2. Confirm: Allow astronauts to validate automatically proposed measurements.
  3. Analyze: Evaluate historical indicators and detect relevant health patterns.
  4. Explain: Generate contextual insights using structured evidence and conversational AI.
  5. Support: Provide selective alerts, reflections, and consultation suggestions.
  6. Engage: Encourage consistent participation through progress tracking and gamification.

Roadmap

Current prototype: Health monitoring backend, device telemetry APIs, personalized insights, conversational assistance, synchronization services, and a mobile interface demonstrating assisted check-ins, voice interactions, and gamification.

Next steps: Validate real device integrations, evaluate monitoring accuracy, and measure time saved during daily check-ins.
